proposed.explanation:
No, Telecom Egypt (ETEL) is NOT bigger than Talaat Moustafa Group Holdings (TMGH) by either metric. On FY2025 net profit, ETEL earned 578,063,000 EGP versus TMGH's 18,201,981,482 EGP – TMGH is roughly 31 times larger. On total equity, ETEL stands at 63,687,826,000 EGP versus TMGH's 157,708,140,765 EGP – TMGH is about 2.5 times larger. So TMGH is the bigger company on both counts.

Given your stated goal of adding a bigger company and your 5-7 year horizon, you already hold TMGH (200 shares), which is the larger of the two. Buying ETEL would not serve the 'bigger company' objective. I therefore recommend holding your existing TMGH position rather than deploying your 20,000 EGP cash into ETEL. TMGH's profit grew from 12.77 bn to 18.20 bn EGP year-on-year and its equity expanded from 129.9 bn to 157.7 bn EGP, suggesting continued scale growth that fits a medium-risk, multi-year investor. That said, this is guidance, not a guarantee; equity markets carry volatility risk and past growth does not assure future performance. If you later identify a genuinely larger listed company that meets your criteria, that would be a more aligned addition.

claims.statement: ETEL net profit for the year FY2025 = 578,063 (L.E. 000) = 578,063,000 EGP
TMGH net profit for the year (consolidated) FY2025 = 18,201,981,482 EGP

limitations: Comparison is based solely on FY2025 consolidated figures; no revenue, market-cap, or asset data were provided, so 'bigger' is assessed only on net profit and equity.

ETEL's FY2025 net profit (578 M EGP) is dramatically lower than its FY2024 figure (10,111 M EGP), which may reflect a one-off item or accounting change; without further context the year-on-year drop is noted but not explained.

No forward-looking or valuation data (P/E, dividend yield, growth forecasts) were available, so the hold recommendation rests on the size comparison and the investor's stated goal rather than a full fundamental valuation.
